content:
Let the required day be \(n\). Spending starts on day 2, so for day \(k\ge 2\):

- Earnings: \(20+(k-1)X\)
- Spending: \(15+(k-2)Y\)

Net balance after \(n\) days:
\[
B_n=20+\sum_{k=2}^n\left(20+(k-1)X-15-(k-2)Y\right)
\]
\[
=5n+15+\frac{n(n-1)}{2}X-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2}Y
\]
Set \(B_n=60\):
\[
5n+15+\frac{n(n-1)}{2}X-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2}Y=60
\]
\[
(n-1)\left(Xn-Y(n-2)\right)=10(9-n)
\]

Thus, without specific values of \(X\) and \(Y\), there is no unique numerical day.

\[
\boxed{\text{No unique day; solve } (n-1)(Xn-Y(n-2))=10(9-n)}
\]
